after.event: Gu Piqiang was hosting guests in his famous Wu-commandery garden when Xianzhi toured the grounds as if no one else were there
after.unresolvedReason: The garden episode is introduced only by 嘗經吳郡 and 時辟彊方集賓友; the chapter supplies no reign year. The previous sourceDate 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 belongs to a different Xianzhi visit and cannot date this scene, and AD 360–396 is not in the passage.

changes.reason: s0271–s0273 date Gu Piqiang’s garden gathering only with 嘗經吳郡 and 時辟彊方集賓友. 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 is a separate Xianzhi visit and is not the date of this scene. AD 360–396 was invented from Xianzhi’s later career and must be removed. The episode remains Gu’s own undated hosting event, marked unresolved rather than given a guessed interval.

Xianzhi’s memorial dates Xie An’s service from 陛下踐阼. 晉書孝武帝紀 records 咸安二年秋七月己未，立為皇太子。是日，簡文帝崩，太子卽皇帝位, the conventional AD 372 accession of Xiaowu. 寧康元年春正月己丑朔，改元 is the AD 373 era-change and is not the accession. Xie An’s contextual attestation must follow that accession year, not 373.
陛下踐阼 in s0352 is Xiaowu’s own accession. The primary annal 咸安二年秋七月己未 dates that accession to conventional AD 372. AD 373 is 寧康元年改元 and must not be substituted as a second or exact accession endpoint.
The accession row must use the same 咸安二年 July date as the annals, conventional AD 372, and not the 寧康元年 era-change of AD 373. Subject, predicate, and non-date value fields stay unchanged.

s0296 安僖皇后立 comes after 俄而卒於官. Using it as Xianzhi’s living attestation in AD 396 treats a later reception as life activity. The installation and the posthumous honors are retained on the empress row, the honor/office rows, and a retrospective reception event, not as a life date.

安僖皇后立 is the empress’s own installation. 晉書安帝紀 dates 立皇后王氏 to 隆安元年二月戊午, conventional AD 397. 太元二十一年 / AD 396 is when she was made heir-consort, a different earlier appointment, and must not date the installation.

The posthumous honor 安僖皇后立，以後父追贈 is the reception at the empress’s installation, dated by 安帝紀 隆安元年二月戊午 to conventional AD 397, not 太元二十一年 / AD 396. The honor itself is kept; only the Western year is corrected. This remains later reception, not Xianzhi’s living office.

After 俄而卒於官 the chapter records 安僖皇后立，以後父追贈侍中、特進、光祿大夫、太宰，諡曰憲. That is later reception of Xianzhi at his daughter’s installation in 隆安元年 (AD 397), not a living attestation in 396. The honors are preserved as a retrospective-reference with receptionType retrospective.

after.event: Xi Tan is identified only as the father of Wang Xianzhi's former wife

changes.reason: s0294 says only 獻之前妻，郗曇女也. That is an undated kinship identification. AD 340–361 is not in this chapter and must not be imported from a full Xi Tan biography.

after.event: Xianzhi's former wife from the Xi clan is recalled only in his deathbed confession of the divorce
after.unresolvedReason: 與郗家離婚 is remembered during 獻之遇疾; the chapter never states the year of the divorce itself. AD 360–386 is a guessed life span, not a source date for the wife's own event.

changes.reason: The divorce is recalled at Xianzhi’s last illness (s0293–s0294) but is not given a year. Dating it AD 360–386 copies a guessed life span onto the former wife. The divorce remains unresolved; the 385–386 window belongs to Xianzhi’s illness and death, not to the marriage’s end.

after.event: An unnamed elder brother of Wang Xianzhi is mentioned only as Jingzhi's father when Jingzhi was made heir

changes.reason: s0297 以兄子靜之嗣 names the brother only as Jingzhi’s father. He has no own dated event. AD 344–386 copies Xianzhi’s conventional life onto him and must be removed. No birth year is inferred from anyone’s traditional inclusive age.

after.event: Wang Jingzhi was made heir after the childless Wang Xianzhi died in office
after.unresolvedReason: 以兄子靜之嗣 follows 俄而卒於官 but names no reign year; exact AD 386 is false precision copied from Xianzhi’s death window.

changes.reason: Jingzhi’s succession is narrated after Xianzhi’s death but without a calendar year. An exact AD 386 endpoint invents precision the clause 以兄子靜之嗣 does not support. The claim is marked unresolved rather than given a closed year or a fabricated 420 end.

after.event: Wang Jingzhi later reached the office of Administrator of Yixing
after.unresolvedReason: 位至義興太守 is an undated career ceiling; AD 386–420 invents a start from Xianzhi’s death and an end at the fall of Eastern Jin, describing activity through a dynasty rather than uncertainty about one event.

changes.reason: 位至義興太守 states only that Jingzhi’s career reached Yixing administrator. It gives no year. AD 386–420 turns a dynasty-length span into a date window and must be removed. The office claim stays, unresolved.

桓玄雅愛其父子書 is undated later reception of the Wang calligraphy. AD 398–404 is Huan Xuan’s political floruit, not a date in this passage, and must not be used as living activity. The appreciation is kept as a retrospective reception event without a fabricated career interval.

s0299 records Huan Xuan’s appreciation of the father-and-son calligraphy as later reception, with no reign year. The event is preserved as retrospective-reference / receptionType retrospective and left undated rather than assigned AD 398–404.

after.event: Wang Xizhi visited Xu Mai after the Lin'an western-hills move and spent whole days there as friends beyond the common world

changes.reason: 永和二年 dates Xu Mai’s move to 臨安西山, not a closed year for Wang Xizhi’s repeated visits in s0317. The visits follow that move, so the only supported Western constraint is onOrAfter AD 346. No end year is invented, and s0317–s0319 remain undated as to a precise visit year.

after.event: Xu Mai visited Guo Pu for a yarrow divination before his capping year
after.unresolvedReason: 未弱冠，嘗造郭璞 gives only a traditional age-stage, not a calendar year; AD 310–324 imports Guo Pu’s external lifespan and disagrees with the AD 320–324 hint window.

changes.reason: The Guo Pu visit is dated only by 未弱冠. That age statement is already kept on claim-889 and is not a Western year. AD 310–324 manufactures endpoints from Guo Pu’s external lifespan and must be stripped. The visit is unresolved.

after.event: Guo Pu cast the yarrow for Xu Mai before Xu Mai's capping year
after.unresolvedReason: The visit is dated only by Xu Mai’s 未弱冠; the chapter never names a reign year, and AD 310–324 is not in the passage.

changes.reason: Guo Pu’s divination has no calendar year in s0304. Importing his external lifespan to make AD 310–324 or AD 320–324 is unsupported. His event remains the undated consultation, marked unresolved.

after.event: Xu Mai's father was still living while Mai kept the Xuansliu hermitage and returned at the new and full moons

changes.reason: 父母尚存 precedes 父母既終, and both precede 遍游名山, 餌術涉三年, and 永和二年. AD 320–346 invents a start year from 未弱冠 and lets the still-alive state run through the 346 move, which contradicts that order. The supported constraint is a one-sided bound before the Yonghe 2 move, with no second endpoint.

after.event: Xu Mai's mother was still living while Mai kept the Xuansliu hermitage and returned at the new and full moons

changes.reason: The mother’s survival is the same 父母尚存 clause. It ends at 既終, which itself stands before the three-year herb stay and the Yonghe 2 move. AD 320 is invented; 346 is the move, not the end of her lifetime. Only a before-AD-346 bound is kept.

父母既終 is the father’s death event, but it is not dated to 永和二年. After the deaths come 遣婦, 遍游名山, and 餌術涉三年, and only then 永和二年移入臨安西山. The death therefore has a one-sided bound before the Yonghe 2 / conventional AD 346 move. No precise death year and no second endpoint are invented.

The same 父母既終 clause is the mother’s death. Attaching AD 346 copies Xu Mai’s later Lin’an move onto her death and ignores the intervening three-year herb stay. The death is bounded only as before that move.

sourceDate.text: 時南海太守鮑靚隱跡潛遁

after.unresolvedReason: 時南海太守鮑靚隱跡潛遁 is only a narrative 'at that time' after the Guo Pu visit; this chapter gives no reign year, and AD 317–340 is not in the passage.

changes.reason: 時 marks Bao Jing’s hiding as contemporaneous with Xu Mai’s search, not as AD 317–340. Replacing one invented career span with another dynasty-length window would repeat the same error. The attestation is unresolved.

sourceDate.text: 陳安世、茅季偉常所遊處

changes.reason: 陳安世、茅季偉常所遊處 is undated mountain lore in Xu Mai’s biography. BC 32–7 imports a Han reign-span as if it were Chen Anshi’s life or active dates. The mention is kept as retrospective reception, not as a dated life attestation.

sourceDate.text: 陳安世、茅季偉常所遊處

changes.reason: The same clause mentions Mao Jiwei only as a former roamer of the Mao-mountain caves. BC 140–87 is an imported Han reign-span, not a date in this chapter. The life window is removed; the place-lore mention is preserved as retrospective reception.
s0309 cites 陳安世 as someone who had commonly roamed the Yuhang/Mao-mountain terrain Xu Mai then occupied. That is retrospective place-lore with no date. No Han biography or life years are added.

茅季偉 is named together with Chen Anshi in the same undated mountain-lore sentence. The later reference is kept as retrospective-reference / receptionType retrospective, without imported Western life dates.

AD 189–220 invents both ends of 漢末 and treats the citation as living activity. 漢末 remains unresolved as a life span; the later reference is kept as retrospective reception dated to the letter after the Lin’an settlement.
